coupling: The NULL-buffer substitution maintenance commit changes how a shallow copy of match data drops copied-subject ownership: it clears that ownership bit only when it is the sole match-data flag. The later get_subject maintenance commit records zero-length copied subjects with a second match-data flag, while allocating a one-byte subject for them. Before the later commit the extra flag is absent, and with only the later edit the original unconditional ownership clear remains. Together, substitution of a successful empty copied match leaves the ownership bit in the internal shallow copy. Substitution frees the copied subject through that copy; freeing the caller-owned match data frees the same allocation again. Repair requires relating the flag added for empty copied subjects to ownership transfer in the earlier substitution change.
